text.p: Here are the leading stories
reported by Lithuania's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not
verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- President Algirdas Brazauskas and other top politicians
declared the income and property of their families.
- Social Security and Labour Minister Irena Degutiene said
funds for disabled people were used without control.
- Parliament approved the appointment of two new deputy
prosecutor generals.
- Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta expects a rating by
Standard & Poor's to be announced in the second half of May.
- McDonalds is to cut prices in Lithuania by average 18
percent from May 2.
RESPUBLIKA
- The chairman of the parliament human rights committee
Emanuelis Zingeris said parliament should debate the abolition
of capital punishment.
- If presidential elections were held tomorrow 26.3 percent
of those polled would vote for U.S. enviroment protection expert
Valdas Adamkus, 24 percent for President Algirdas Brazauskas and
13.8 percent for Arturas Paulauskas, an opinion poll showed.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene told the
newspaper that membership in the European Union and the
privatisation of big transport, energy and communication
companies were two inseparable things.
VERSLO ZINIOS
- The chairman of the parliament finance and budget
committee Elvyra Kunevichiene expects that VAT will be cut at
the start of next year. The government promised in its election
plan to cut VAT from 18 to 16 percent in the first half of 1997.
- The governor of the Bank of Lithuania Reinoldijus
Sharkinas tells the newspaper that he thinks the number of banks
will fall to 6-8 banks before the end of the year.
- The Bank of Lithuania said it is ready to start repo
auctions only when necessary.
- The newspaper publishes financial reports for 1996 of six
banks and analyses their activities.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 22 35 18
